facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of a gradually enlarging right breast swelling
no history of tuberculosis or tuberculous contact
no family history of cancer
a tender swelling in the outer half of the right breast with overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction
a mobile ipsilateral axillary lymph node measured 2.5 cm
no nipple discharge
inflammatory markers and cultures was strictly normal
Ultrasonography and mammography showed an ACR-4 lesion in the supero-external quadrant of the right breast
a skin fistula developed with pus extruding and an “orange peel” appearance of the overlying skin
Breast MRI revealed multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls throughout the gland, extending to the skin, with peripheral enhancement
